edge_cases: Missing required fields in the JSON payload may cause a server error.
Providing a non‑integer year or book_id results in a 500 error.
Searching with an empty keyword returns all books.
Updating or deleting a non‑existent book_id still returns a success message but affects no rows.
Large keyword strings may degrade performance.
Invalid query parameters (e.g., non‑numeric year) may cause SQLite errors.
contract.intent: Provide a RESTful API for managing a collection of books stored in a SQLite database, allowing clients to add, search, update, delete, and retrieve books by year.
invariants: Each book record has a unique integer id primary key.
The books table contains columns: id, title, author, year.
Year values are stored as integers.
HTTP methods correspond to their intended CRUD operation.
The API does not alter files other than library.db.
io_behavior: POST /add_book with JSON {title, author, year} returns 201 and a success message.
GET /search_books?keyword=... returns 200 and a JSON array of matching books.
PUT /update_book/<book_id> with JSON {title?, author?, year?} returns 200 and a success message.
DELETE /delete_book/<book_id> returns 200 and a success message.
GET /get_books_by_year?year=... returns 200 and a JSON array of books from that year.
All responses are JSON-encoded and use standard HTTP status codes.
side_effects: Inserts a new row into the books table on /add_book.
Reads rows from the database on /search_books and /get_books_by_year.
Commits transactions to persist changes in library.db.
Opens and closes a SQLite connection for each request.

rationale: Routes and basic CRUD work, but error handling deviates from contract (non‑existent updates/deletes return 404, invalid types return 400), cursor context manager is invalid causing runtime failures, and edge‑case expectations (500 errors, success on missing rows) are not met.
